High level: Redwood charges each request rounded up to a fixed quantum, with an additional per-call floor and a contextual amortization rule for very long context windows. Those three levers explain the numbers you saw. I'll summarize with a concise worked example below and attach a small spreadsheet with line-by-line math (pricing_workbook_greenline.xlsx) and the sample invoice we generated (sample_invoice_v2.pdf).

--- Below is the short worked example we promised (numbers are illustrative based on your export):

Example inputs (from usage rows):
- Short interactive call A: prompt 80 tokens, completion 40 tokens => raw tokens 120
- Short interactive call B: prompt 140 tokens, completion 60 tokens => raw tokens 200
- Long job L: prompt 6,400 tokens, completion 900 tokens => raw tokens 7,300

Redwood billing parameters for your pilot (current config):
- Quantum: 64 tokens (charges round up to nearest 64-token block)
- Per-call floor: 256 tokens (minimum billed per request unless overridden by pilot concession)
- Context amortization window: 7 days for long-context reuse — long contexts are eligible for amortization if the same conversation reuses cached KV state; amortized cost is applied as a proportional allocation across active requests that reuse the cache.

How each call is calculated:
- Call A: raw 120 => round up to nearest 64 => ceil(120/64)=2 blocks => 128 charged. Enforce floor 256 => billed 256 tokens.
- Call B: raw 200 => ceil(200/64)=4 blocks => 256 charged. Floor 256 => billed 256 tokens.
- Long job L: raw 7,300 => ceil(7300/64)=115 blocks => 115*64=7,360 tokens charged. Because it's a long-context run we additionally evaluate amortization: if this job populates a KV cache that is reused by N subsequent short calls in the same 7-day window, we may allocate part of the 7,360 across those N calls rather than billing it entirely to the single request. Without reuse: billed 7,360 tokens.

Net billed tokens for this sample set (no amortization / no concession): 256 + 256 + 7,360 = 7,872 tokens.

If we applied a 1-month pilot concession (waive per-call floor for first billing period):
- Call A would be billed 128 (quantum only), Call B 256, Long job still 7,360 => total 7,744 tokens, a ~1.6% reduction in this toy example. The largest wins come from waiving floors on many small calls at scale.

I'll let Karthik add a bit more about amortization math and any edge cases we should call out.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@greenlinehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify how short/long calls are bucketed on pilot invoice

Thanks — quick follow-up with more precise math and the amortization example. I'll keep this non-technical for finance and then include a short section for SRE/devs.

1) Rounding/quantum: we use a 64-token quantum for the pilot SKU you signed up for. The invoice rounds each request up to the nearest quantum before applying the per-call floor. Mathematically: billed_tokens = max(per_call_floor, quantum * ceil(raw_tokens / quantum)).

2) Per-call floor: the floor (256 tokens) protects against extreme micropayment churn. Floors are applied at the request level; streaming/chunked requests are treated as a single logical call if they share the same top-level request id.

3) Context amortization example (this is where you can see savings):
- Suppose a long job L (7,360 charged tokens after rounding) loads a large document into the KV cache. Over the following 7 days we observe 40 short calls that reuse that cache (each short call has raw tokens ~150). Rather than charging the full 7,360 only to the original request, we allocate the long job's charged tokens across the reuse cohort. Allocation rule (pilot config): 50% of the long job's charged tokens are attributed to a shared context bucket and the remaining 50% stay on the originating request. The shared bucket is then split equally across the reuse cohort.

Using that rule: shared portion = 7,360 * 0.5 = 3,680. If 40 short calls reused the cache, each gets an allocation of 3,680/40 = 92 tokens (added to their individual billed tokens, before floor/quantum).

So a sample short call with raw 120 tokens would be:
- quantum rounding: ceil(120/64)*64 = 128
- add amortized share: +92 => 220 => ceil(220/64)*64 = 256 => floor keeps it at 256. If floor were waived during the pilot the math would be: 128 + 92 = 220 => round up to 256 anyway (so some amortization still gets rounded up). The amortization materially helps when there are many reuse calls — per-request floor still bites on very small counts.

4) Edge cases / notes for GreenLine:
- If reuse cohort is small (<8 calls), amortization bluntly won't offset the per-call floor; consider temporary floor reduction to 128 for month 1.
- If you do long-batch jobs that do not reuse cache, they will not be amortized — they'll be charged in full to that request.
- Streaming completions that are part of the same user-visible request are consolidated; multiple internal fragments are not billed as separate per-call floors.

Operational ask: if you want us to simulate your first-month bill with (a) current config, (b) floor waived, (c) floor reduced to 128, we can run the spreadsheet and return three invoice views. We can also annotate the sample_invoice_v2.pdf line-by-line.

-Karthik
